newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DOLLAR TO SPUR WOLTERS, STERLING TO BRAKE REED ELS.
newsitem.headline: DOLLAR TO SPUR WOLTERS, STERLING TO BRAKE REED ELS.

text.p: Currency effects are expected to tug interim earnings due next week from professional publishers Wolters Kluwer and Reed Elsevier in opposite directions.
Analysts expect the firm dollar to contribute to a rise in first-half net profit of almost 20 percent for Wolters Kluwer which will report results on Tuesday.
But sterling's strength is seen holding back first half earnings growth to around six percent at Anglo-Dutch Reed Elsevier which reports on Thursday.
Analysts forecast Wolters Kluwer's first-half net profit from ordinary operations at 235-253 million guilders, with a consensus at 245 million, up from 206 million a year earlier.
They estimate Reed Elsevier's headline pre-tax profit at 423-460 million sterling, with a consensus at 441 million, versus 416 million in the first half of 1996.
Wolters Kluwer is expected to return to its familiar path of double-digit annual earnings per share growth at a slightly faster rate than its own official forecast of 15 percent.
Earnings growth slowed to six percent in 1996 due to accounting changes linked to its $1.9 billion acquisition of U.S. tax publisher CCH, but it stressed this was temporary.
The CCH buy lifted North America's share of group sales and profits to around 30 percent from 10, so Wolters Kluwer is well placed to benefit from the dollar's rise in recent months.

Analysts said first-half results would also reflect a continuing improvement of margins at CCH, good organic growth at other Wolters Kluwer businesses and contributions from a string of smaller niche publishers acquired since the CCH deal.
Analysts said Reed Elsevier's businesses were also performing well in local currency terms but that earnings would be held back by the translation into sterling.
The currency effect is highlighted by the fact that first half earnings per share in guilders for Elsevier -- the group's Dutch parent company -- are expected to rise some 20 per cent.

Investment in on-line electronic delivery systems is also holding back the pace of earnings growth, though analysts say this will strengthen Reed Elsevier in the long term. Recent acquisitions in scientific, legal and business publishing are expected to boost earnings from the second half of 1997.

After consistently outperforming the Dutch market over the previous 10 years, Wolters Kluwer and Elsevier shares lagged a 33 percent rise in the AEX index in the first half of 1997 with relatively modest rises of four and 12 percent respectively.
In July they performed more in line with the 14 percent rise of the index, possibly aided by Outperformer ratings for both stocks and for Reed issued by analysts at Goldman Sachs.
Andre Moons at ING Barings said he expected Wolters Kluwer and Elsevier to re-establish their credentials as market outperformers and rates them both a Buy.
"After the severe underperformance so far this year their current valuations are certainly not overstretched," he said.
